title: Guptill Explains Architectural Shadows
content: In this diagram fromWatercolor Painting Step-By-Step, Arthur Guptill shares some insights about shadows.He points out that shadows aren't just darker versions of the local colors, nor are they necessarily a bluer version of those colors. Rather there is often a shift in color within the shadow.In diagrams 6, 7, and 8, the planes that face downward tend to be warmer because of the color of the ground, and the vertical surfaces at the bottom margin of the shadow are more blue or violet because they are filled more with blue skylight.------Diagram fromWatercolor Painting Step-By-Step, Arthur Guptill
